headline: Attacking possession lost: compare the linked alternatives
significance_reason: A logged attacking advance was followed within five seconds by an opposing recovery and an explicit loss of possession.
synthetic_scenario_assumptions: All identities and ratings are fictional; synthetic ratings are uncalibrated indices.
Home attacks along +x on the authored 105 x 68 metre pitch. Positions, velocities and ball ownership are authored, not recovered from tracking.
The carry record anchors this hypothetical starting location. The four-second rollout and 1200ms adaptation are model time, not a reconstruction of event time.
One attacker, one defender and one stationary supporting teammate; separate replay events are not forced to match simulation outcomes.

comparison_evidence.summary: In the authored scenario, wide right ended without friendly possession; release pass ended with friendly possession and improved the modeled tactical objective. This does not guarantee a real match outcome.
comparison_evidence.reason: release_pass improves the lexicographic objective from (false, false, 0, 0) to (true, true, 12, 11); inspect alternative:release_pass opponent-decision and movement events for the spatial evidence.

limitations: Fictional attributes and uncalibrated parameters; no probabilities, expected goals or claims about real athletes.
Two active players and a stationary optional receiver; no collisions, spin, aerial ball, stamina, fouls, goalkeeper, goals or full team tactics.
Interception checks the ball segment against the defender's end-of-tick position. Counter feasibility is a horizon screen, not proof of interception before ball arrival.
Passes aim at a fixed destination; one-two returns may become loose when the moving receiver cannot stop in time. In-flight or loose balls do not count as settled possession.
This spatial scenario performs no Law 11 offence assessment; the existing offside-position endpoint remains separate.
This counterfactual is an authored synthetic scenario, not recovered match tracking or a real success probability. A missing correction means no strictly better feasible branch was found.
